_comment: EXECUTOR session permissions. Command servers only -- no watchdog rule here, so a config mistake that leaked the watchdog server into this session would still prompt on every monitoring call instead of running silently. Bash and Read are explicitly denied: the executor's source of truth is the contract/registry/pose tool calls on the command servers, never the raw registry or task YAML files (and never their comments) read directly off disk or via shell. Task/Agent are denied for the same reason and are not redundant with Bash/Read: a subagent runs under its OWN permissions, so an executor that can spawn one can have it read the registry off disk and report back, bypassing every deny rule here. Observed 2026-09-02: the executor spawned an Explore subagent to 'find and dump model registry' instead of calling get_rendered_task. Write/Edit are denied because the executor has no business modifying the repo mid-run; WebFetch/WebSearch because a scored run's inputs must come from the cell, not the internet.
_run_params_comment: RUN PARAMETERS -- edit these two before a run; they are the only knobs here that change behaviour rather than permissions. model: an alias ('opus', 'sonnet', 'haiku', 'fable') or a full id ('claude-sonnet-5'). effortLevel: one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Both are read by Claude Code from this file because run_executor.sh passes it with --settings, and a --settings file outranks ~/.claude/settings.json. The launcher echoes both values at startup; record them with the run (see RUN.md step 3). Deleting effortLevel restores the model's own default ('auto'); there is no literal 'auto' value to write. Currently BOTH roles run claude-sonnet-5 at low effort, matched to watchdog.settings.json. low suits this role on its own merits: the executor's turns are mechanical -- one instruction-driven skill call at a time -- which is the same reasoning that puts reasoning_effort at low in agents/config/executor_agent.yaml for the API path. Those yaml files are a DIFFERENT path (run_agent.py, provider openai) and their model/reasoning_effort fields do not affect a Claude Code run; this file is the one that does. A --effort or --model flag, and the CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL / ANTHROPIC_MODEL env vars, all outrank this file.
